trip.note: The bag and the market trip (TODO M5, M6, M11). What the farmer carries to the village: the bag holds load units (the weights of rules/45-weight.json; a normal thing is 1). Capacity = the best carrying thing you own (devices: node id -> load units), at least `base` (what fits in your arms). Packing does not take things out of the store: packed things stay there, marked, and can be unpacked for free. Strength (the wellbeing parameter, 0.5 at the start and frozen until chapter 2) carries more: above `strength.from` every point of strength adds `strength.perPoint` of the capacity (full strength: +30%), never less than the plain capacity, in whole load units. A trip costs `energy.base` x the errand multiplier (boots: energy:errand) x what a better road saves (roadSaving per road level above 1, never below roadFloor) x the trip multiplier (a borrowed donkey, a favour: energy:trip), rounded up, at least `energy.min`, and exactly one Time Quiz question; the way back from the village is one more Time Quiz question and no energy.

square.note: The village square as its own screen (money-market/07): a mockup made from pictures the game already has. While the farmer is in the village, this scene stands where the farm was, and the window below it shows the stall that was tapped. backdrop: a painted picture assets/<backdrop>.png, used as the whole scene once it exists (pictures/04); until then the ground and the deco pictures below make the scene (no sky: the ground reaches the top edge). ground: the map of the ground's diamond tiles (ui/square_ground.gd; the pictures are in assets/square_tiles/): rows is one string per row, one letter per cell, letters separated by spaces; row 0 is the top, a row beyond the map repeats the last row and a cell beyond a row's end repeats the row's last letter; kinds says what a letter is (files: its pictures, one is picked per cell by a stable hash of the cell; flip: drawn mirrored). 8 cells span the scene's width, each row sits a quarter of a cell lower than the one above and every odd row is shifted right by half a cell: in an even row (0, 2, …) cell c is centred on x = c cells (the first and the last are half outside the scene; 9 cells), in an odd row on c + 0.5 cells (8 cells); the scene above the window is about 15 rows high, the whole screen about 43 (the map has 45 rows). A tile taller than a slab (tulips, lupins) is drawn with its slab where the row puts it and its flowers standing up over the row above. Letters in use: g grass, f daisies and clover, a autumn leaves, u tulips, l lupins, v seedlings, t tilled soil, s packed soil, n sand, c cobbles, m mossy, r wet, h straw, y sandy fans, p big pale slabs, b red brick, k plank stage, e/E and d/D edges to grass and soil, j/J grass to soil. An edge tile has cobbles in its lower half and grass or soil in its upper half: e and d have the grass or soil at the upper RIGHT, E and D (the same pictures, mirrored) at the upper LEFT, so a border of grass or soil lies diagonally above the cobbles, never below them; without a ground map the flat ground tile named by `ground` (a picture's name) is used. Every picture stands with the middle of its lower edge at x, y (shares of the scene's width and height) and is w of the scene's width wide (never taller than maxH of its height). stalls: what can be tapped; id is a stall a part of the interface registered (ui/square.gd add_stall: sell, seeds, traders, orders, board) or home (the walk home); first: the stall open on arrival when the farmer came for none in particular; art '' makes a stall an invisible tap area of w x h (for a painted backdrop). Swapping the mockup for painted pictures needs only this block and the picture files. People (rules/58-people.json): points are named places (shares of the scene) the villagers stroll between, in straight lines, so choose them so no line crosses a stall; figureH is a figure's height as a share of the scene's width (as the stalls' w is); a stall's seller {dx, dy} is where its seller stands, as shares of the scene's width and height from the stall's x, y.
